newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks resume record closing run.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks resume record closing run.

text.p: Swiss shares ended an active session on Wednesday at a record close, regaining strength after a closing dip the day before ended a four-day record run.
But marked gains were limited to a handful of blue chips.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closed up 86.3 to a record 5,662.4.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 46.05 to 3,571.55, also a record.
Novartis, up 72 Swiss francs at 2,338, led the actives. Nestle, Swiss Re, Zurich Group and ABB were also strong gainers, helped by buy recommendations, traders said.
UBS rose five to 1,639 Swiss francs, CS Group and Roche were steady, Alusuisse lost 12 to 1,506.
Total trade volume was 2.76 billion Swiss francs.
Dealers said gains in ABB, Nestle, Novartis, Swiss Re and Zurich counted for the major part of the index rise.
Wall Street's firm trend supported sentiment.
Dealers said Wall Street was an important factor for the Swiss market's short-term outlook but that a growing number of market participants believed the SMI would rise as high as 6,000 points anyway.
Among leading shares Novartis was seen having potential for One dealer said he expected Novartis to rise to 2,800 Swiss francs. Nestle was seen moving above 2,000 and ABB was expected to reach 2,500.
Second-tiers saw Sulzer, Buehrle, Ascom and Sika higher. In the transport sector Kuehne&Nagel and Danzas were in demand.
Zurich Group were pushed higher by speculation that the group was close to acquiring U.S. portfolio manager Scudder.
Chart analysts said the share was expected to break out of its current range of 550/570 francs and reach 600/620 francs.
